hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.
note: seeds best-so-far and the convergence window; does not start the stall counter

hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise FM with LightGBM over base5 plus within-user duration features and out-of-fold item/author rate aggregates will beat the 0.6016 baseline by a wide margin.
rationale: The FM only has user_id x video_id interactions and the organizers show that saturates; trees can use continuous, within-user-varying signals (item long-view rate, author rate, log duration, duration percentile inside the user's own list) that the categorical FM frame cannot express at all. Item popularity/quality rates are the single strongest within-user discriminator on KuaiRand because 99.9% of valid videos are seen in train, so the out-of-fold rates transfer.
expected_gain_derivation: [HIGH_COVERAGE] means the train-window item long-view rate is defined for essentially every valid row, so it acts as a per-item prior that varies inside every user's ~6-row list [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]; [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD] only rules out STATIC categorical fields, not outcome-derived rates, so their null result does not bound this. Item-rate priors typically move GAUC from ~0.667 to ~0.72 and nDCG@5 similarly on logged-impression re-ranking; averaging gives ~0.655, i.e. +0.055 over 0.6016. I discount for the fact that trees handle raw high-cardinality user_id/video_id poorly, so most of the lift must come from the aggregates.

block_justifications.base5: It is the exact frame the 0.6016 baseline uses, so keeping it makes the model-family change interpretable and retains tab/dur_bucket which vary within a user's list.
block_justifications.dur_feats: Duration percentile rank is computed within the user's own list, so it is a within-user-varying signal [WITHIN_USER_RANKING] and duration bias is on the organizers' unexplored list [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED].
block_justifications.item_agg: Out-of-fold train-window video/author long-view and click rates are the per-item quality prior that the FM frame cannot express, and [HIGH_COVERAGE] guarantees they are populated for nearly all valid rows.

hypothesis: Switching LightGBM from pointwise binary to lambdarank with training groups capped at 6 consecutive rows per user (matching the ~5.6-row valid lists) will beat both the FM baseline and the pointwise LightGBM run.
rationale: The metric is a within-user ordering metric, but every model tried so far optimises an independent per-row likelihood [POINTWISE_BASELINE]; lambdarank's gradient is proportional to the NDCG change of swapping a pair inside a group, so it spends capacity exactly on the pairs the metric counts. Capping the group at 6 rows makes the training list length and the position discount match the evaluation list length instead of a 43.5-row list whose discount is dominated by ranks the valid metric never sees [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH]. Truncation level 6 keeps the whole short list in the pair pool, which is what nDCG@5 over ~6 items requires [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]. Feature frame is held identical to iteration 1 so the score difference is attributable to the objective+grouping change alone [ONE_CHANGE_PER_SPEC].
expected_gain_derivation: Iteration 1 with this exact feature frame scored 0.59866 pointwise, i.e. the frame is roughly baseline-equivalent, so any movement here is the loss change. [POINTWISE_BASELINE] plus [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] list loss as the single largest untried lever, and [SHORT_EVAL_LISTS] means a pairwise objective on 6-item lists is close to directly optimising the reported score. Typical pointwise->pairwise deltas on short-list NDCG are 0.01-0.04; I take the middle, +0.020 over the current best 0.6014 (~0.621). Far above the 0.0008 seed-noise floor [SEED_NOISE].

block_justifications.dur_feats: Duration percentile rank is computed within the user's own list, making it a within-user-varying signal, and duration bias is an explicitly unexplored direction [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED].
block_justifications.item_agg: Out-of-fold video/author long-view rates are the per-item quality prior that varies across a user's candidates, and [HIGH_COVERAGE] means 99.9% of valid videos have a populated value; held constant vs iteration 1 for attribution.

hypothesis: Adding the cross_agg block (user x author affinity, user x tag affinity, duration relative to the user's own long-viewed duration) to the winning lambdarank/chunk-6 configuration will produce the largest single gain so far, because it is the first genuinely personalised, within-user-varying information source tried.
rationale: Everything scored so far is either a user-constant term (user_id first-order, user_agg) or an item-global prior (item_agg, video/author rates). [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT] means the former cannot reorder a list at all, and an item-global prior gives every user the same ordering of the same candidates, so it can only recover the population-average preference. cross_agg is the only available block whose value depends jointly on the user and the candidate while still varying across that user's ~6 rows, i.e. it is the tree-frame analogue of the user_id x video_id interaction the organizers say carries most of the signal, but generalised through author/tag/duration so it survives for unseen (user,video) pairs. It is also the closest available proxy to the organizers' unexplored 'user behaviour sequence' direction, since duration-relative-to-history is a summary of past watching behaviour.
expected_gain_derivation: [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] lists behaviour sequences and duration-bias modelling as untouched, and [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD] shows that the only feature family already measured (static side fields) gave ~0.000, which does not bound a personalised interaction family. The objective change alone bought +0.0016 over the FM baseline (0.60141 -> 0.60297) on an unchanged frame, so a frame change of comparable-or-larger information content plausibly buys several times that. [CEILING] leaves 0.2455 of headroom above current best, so 0.008 is ~3% of remaining headroom - a deliberately modest fraction. Well above [SEED_NOISE] 0.0008, and enough on its own to clear the 0.60341 window threshold from [CONVERGENCE_MECHANICS].
